source_title: 'Commit to ballot paper': Congress dares PM Modi after his 'how many seats' swipe over MLC results - The Times of India
source_excerpt: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Wednesday took a swipe at the Congress over its dismal performance in the MLC polls held across four states. The grand old party which failed to win a single seat in the polls, hit back at PM Modi over his âballot paperâ remark and challenged him to commit to holding all future Lok Sabha and assembly elections using ballot papers.The back-and-forth began when the Prime Minister in a post on X, wrote, "MLC elections in 28 seats across 4 big states - Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Bihar and Karnataka. Elections held using ballot papers. Guess how many seats Congress won?"Congress Rajya Sabha member Pawan Khera hit back at PM Modi, asking him to demonstrate confidence in the BJPâs prowess by committing to ballot paper voting in all future Lok Sabha and assembly elections.In a post on X, Khera demanded the suspension of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and the restoration of 13.3 crore voters "deleted illegally"."If Narendra Modi is so confident that EVMs have no bearing on election results, let him prove his confidence in the BJPâs electoral prowess through action, not rhetoric," he wrote."1. Terminate Gyanesh Gupta. 4. Repeal the law that gives life long immunity to Gyanesh Gupta," Khera wrote.BJP national president Nitin Nabin also took a dig at the grand old party, saying the party would continue to struggle for survival under Rahul Gandhi's leadership. The results also saw the Congress lose its sitting Bengaluru Teachersâ constituency to the JD(S).The prime minister's reference to ballot papers comes amid the opposition's repeated allegations of irregularities in electronic voting machines (EVMs) and demands for greater transparency in the electoral process.The Congress suffered its biggest setback in Karnataka, where the BJP retained three seats and the JD(S) wrested Bengaluru Teachersâ from the ruling party.JD(S) candidate A P Ranganath defeated sitting Congress MLC Puttanna by 908 votes, securing 10,810 votes against his rival's 9,902.The BJP retained the North-East Teachersâ, South-East Graduatesâ and West Graduatesâ constituencies.
